source_audit.finding: The source has closed interval domains; the graph compiler has open domains. Rational clipping with positive determinant and six strict linear inequalities gives the exact closed unit input/output restriction. These inequalities hold whenever all coefficient deviations from identity are below 1/4, in particular when their squared sum is below 1/16, and are stable under the adjugate inverse. A finite family loses at most two endpoint images per map on passing to the open domain. Spectral-gap and generator-existence proofs are not supplied by these algebraic and measure bridges.

proof_scope: In progress. R1757 proves the exact rational unit-domain and measure adapters for the source expansion construction. RationalUnitMobius uses rational coefficients, positive determinant and six strict linear inequalities. Clipping computes lo=max(0,-b/a) and hi=min(1,(d-b)/(a-c)); the interval is nondegenerate and is exactly the closed set where input and output lie in [0,1]. The coefficient conditions are preserved by adjugate inversion, cover opposite translations and identity, and follow from coefficient deviations below 1/4 or squared sum below 1/16. The finite augmented source family is constructed and its image union decomposed exactly. For every finite rational map family and arbitrary input set, replacing closed domains by open domains removes only finitely many endpoint images, hence preserves outer measure and real measure exactly. Restricted source expansion therefore supplies the existing epsilon/2 all-size graph expansion and the same complete native arbitrary-computation, CutIneq and MStar conclusions. No analytic expansion or generator-existence claim is inferred from these adapters.
